title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
statement:
An arithmetic expression is written in **postfix** (reverse Polish) notation as a sequence of `n` tokens. Each token is either an integer (possibly negative) or one of the four operators `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`.

To evaluate it, read the tokens from left to right. An integer is remembered; an operator takes the two most recently remembered values `a` (earlier) and `b` (later), computes `a op b`, and remembers the result in their place. For example, `6 2 /` means `6 / 2`, and `8 3 -` means `8 - 3`.

Integer division **truncates toward zero** (so `7 / 2 = 3` and `-7 / 2 = -3`).

The expression is guaranteed to be valid: it never divides by zero, and exactly one value is left at the end. Print that value.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the integer `n`, the number of tokens.
The second line contains the `n` tokens separated by single spaces.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the value of the expression.
constraints: Every integer token has absolute value at most 10^9
Every intermediate result has absolute value at most 10^9

examples.explanation: A single number is its own value.

hints: An operator always applies to the two values produced most recently. Which data structure gives you the most recent items first?
Push integers on a stack; on an operator, pop the right operand first, then the left one, and push the result.

Take care with division: the language's own `/` or `//` may round toward negative infinity or produce a float. Truncate toward zero explicitly. Also tell the token `-` apart from a negative number like `-5`.
